narratives.Description: Module 6 solution and Lab 7 Task 5 disagree on the proposed-scope filename
narratives.Overview:
## Situation

Module 6 O6.2 tells the learner to keep the proposed-scope artifact for Lab 7 Task 5. The explained Module 6 solution records this worked path:

`<lab root>/xbrief/proposed/2026-01-15-northstar-delayed-route-preview.xbrief.json`

Lab 7 Task 5 hard-codes a different path and fails closed if that file is missing:

```sh
authored="$first_root/xbrief/proposed/2026-01-15-your-proposed-scope.xbrief.json"
...
test -f "$authored"
```

The Windows Lab 7 route uses the same `2026-01-15-your-proposed-scope.xbrief.json` name.

I completed Module 6 from the worksheet, compared with the explained solution, then followed Lab 7 Task 5. The two pages disagree on the only filename the helper checks.

## Pain

A mid-level engineer using the explained solution as the comparison surface will write the artifact under the solution’s filename. Lab 7 then fails at `test -f "$authored"` even though the JSON is valid. The recovery table talks about invalid JSON and Acceptance types; it does not mention a filename mismatch with the Module 6 solution.

I had to ignore the solution’s “worked value” and use the lab’s placeholder name. That undercuts the Module 6 instruction to keep “this exact file.”

## Proposed fix

Pick one filename and use it in all four places:

- Module 6 solution structural-record path
- Lab 7 Task 5 `authored=` assignment
- Lab 7 Windows route `$Authored`
- Lab 7 explained solution, if it names a path

`2026-01-15-northstar-delayed-route-preview.xbrief.json` matches the story ID. If the lab keeps the placeholder name, the Module 6 solution should say Task 5 requires that exact filename.

Round 1 fresh open critique of issue 52. Dispatch SHA `19f2b3dd829d089519a22cfeaba8d0bbd7fb9e23`. Id ceiling 5768898228 (Stop 1 write-back, inclusive).

Re-verified P1 at that SHA with `git show` / `git grep` / `node scripts/verify-module-6.mjs` (exit 0). Learner-facing hardcodes of the two basenames are exactly four sites:

- `solutions/module-06-creating-well-shaped-work.md:213` — `2026-01-15-northstar-delayed-route-preview.xbrief.json`
- `labs/07-scope-lifecycle.md:236` — `authored=` `2026-01-15-your-proposed-scope.xbrief.json` then `test -f`
- `labs/07-scope-lifecycle.md:415` — PowerShell `$Authored` same placeholder basename
- `solutions/lab-07-scope-lifecycle.md:186` — Lab 7 explained-solution Artifact path, same placeholder basename

The only other hit is `scripts/verify-module-6.test.mjs:188`, a fake-lab fixture, not a fifth learner path.

## 1. sharpens-framing — Name the Lab 7 drop-in winner on the recut

Evidence. Three of the four learner sites already share `2026-01-15-your-proposed-scope.xbrief.json`. The Module 6 solution structural-record cell is the outlier, and it sits next to the sentence “Lab 7 Task 5 checks this exact artifact.” Lab 7 Task 5 is titled “your own proposed scope” and already treats the file as a third record beside `2026-01-15-fictional-delivery.xbrief.json` and `2026-01-15-fictional-cancel.xbrief.json`. The same solution page’s JSON example keeps `plan.id` `northstar.delayed-route-preview`; Module 6 walkthrough action 3 uses that id (`curriculum/modules/06-creating-well-shaped-work.md:322-323`); Module 4 teaches `YYYY-MM-DD-descriptive-slug.xbrief.json` (`curriculum/modules/04-xbrief-as-durable-state.md:111`). `xbrief:verify` is invoked with `--out` of a caller-chosen path, so filename and `plan.id` are allowed to differ; Task 5 is already a copy-into-a-fixed-path step.

Failure mode. “Pick one filename” leaves the implementer with two recuts of different size. Recutting the Module 6 solution cell to the placeholder makes the structural-record sentence true and leaves the fail-closed helper, Windows route, and Lab 7 solution already aligned. Recutting the Lab 7 family to the northstar slug also aligns P1, and it moves the unix assignment, the Windows `$Authored` line, and the Lab 7 solution path together. Part B still asks for “one story ID and title,” so a hardcoded drop-in path remains a rename-at-copy for any learner whose scratch name differs.

Disposition. Bind with an explicit winner. Keep `2026-01-15-your-proposed-scope.xbrief.json` as the Lab 7 drop-in basename and recut `solutions/module-06-creating-well-shaped-work.md:213` to that same basename so the “checks this exact artifact” sentence is true. Recutting the Lab 7 unix, Windows, and explained-solution paths to the northstar slug also binds; that is the larger move, and it is the one that follows the Module 4 slug convention plus the walkthrough id.

Road-not-taken. A glob of `xbrief/proposed/*.xbrief.json` minus the two supplied fixtures would be a new selection mechanism. The existing `test -f` / `Test-Path` check is the control; unify the string it already uses.

Steelman. The northstar slug is the filename a walkthrough-follower would derive from Module 4 plus `northstar.delayed-route-preview`. Recutting the solution cell to the placeholder makes that structural-record path differ from the JSON `plan.id` on the same page. The verdict would flip if the drop-in filename were required to match `plan.id`.

## 2. sharpens-framing — Lock the shared basename in `requireStructuralEvidenceContract`

Evidence. `scripts/verify-module-6.mjs` `requireStructuralEvidenceContract` already receives Module 6 solution prose, Lab 7 prose, and `labCommands`. It asserts Task 5 command shape against `"$authored"` and keeps the two supplied fixture names. It does not compare the Module 6 solution Artifact-path basename with Lab 7 `authored=`, Windows `$Authored`, or the Lab 7 solution path. `labCommands` is joined from fences whose language is `sh|bash|zsh|console` (`scripts/verify-module-6.mjs:405-408`); the PowerShell fence is outside that string. `node scripts/verify-module-6.mjs` exits 0 on this SHA while the four learner sites disagree.

Failure mode. A four-file prose recut can land and later split again with a green Module 6 contract. The Windows path can drift from the unix path with the current extractor.

Disposition. Extend that existing function so one basename appears in all four learner sites, including the PowerShell `$Authored` line read from the lab file. Update `scripts/verify-module-6.test.mjs` only as needed for the new assertion. The fixture at line 188 is not a fifth learner-facing path.

## 3. footnote — Lab 7 explained solution already names the path

`solutions/lab-07-scope-lifecycle.md:186` already publishes `2026-01-15-your-proposed-scope.xbrief.json`. The fourth recut site is required.

## 4. footnote — Missing-file recovery is leftover after the identity recut

Lab 7 recovery names `invalid JSON`, Acceptance-type, and missing top-level key (`labs/07-scope-lifecycle.md:350-352`). Unix Task 5 uses `test -f "$authored"` with no diagnostic. Windows already throws `Write your Module 6 proposed scope to $Authored first.` (`:416`). After the four-site identity recut, solution-followers are relieved. A later wrong-basename miss is still visible in the Task 5 assignment line.
